Q: How do incomplete relevance labels and unanswerable questions distort retrieval metrics?
A:
Retrieval metrics assume a relevance definition and a judged candidate population. If a useful document is unjudged, treating it as irrelevant can penalize a legitimate result. Conversely, weak labels can reward a related passage that does not answer the question.

Include unanswerable, conflicting and permission-denied cases with their proper expected behavior. Report candidate depth and ranking cutoffs, inspect disagreements and distinguish missing labels from actual failures. A single aggregate score cannot describe every operational risk.
Why: A query has two valid supporting documents but only one is labeled. A new retriever returns the other document and appears worse until the judgment set is reviewed against the same relevance criteria.
Risk: Unjudged data can be mistaken for negative ground truth.
Trade: Broader judgment improves validity at review cost; report uncertainty and sampling scope.
Try: Review a metric regression and separate true misses from incomplete labels.
